title: The owner's plain-word Opus ask in his own typed message lifts the Opus refusal
why: Owner chat Nov 3 19:47 CST, "a read plain asks", to triage's question: when he says "send opus agents" or "some opus judges" in chat, the spawn just runs, without the keyword `opus 2h` or `override`. He asked 19:31 CST: "i thought we fixed this ... when i type saying send opus agents it just works its just quotable my words and the guard lets it through".
note: Ruling home: decision owner-override (rewrite in place: a plain Opus ask in the owner's own typed prompt grants an Opus override, beside the keyword forms) and decision agent-model-cap. It adds to the Oct 29 ruling that a grant can live on the roadmap step (step opus-grant-on-step); that route stays. Shape for the lane: the UserPromptSubmit hook reads only the owner's typed prompt, never agent text or tool output; a model judge (call_judge) reads the sentence, so "maybe opus?" or a question grants nothing; the grant is kind opus with the owner's words in guard.log, for the session and its agents, with a bounded time and the role the words name, else every role. Red tests first: a plain ask lifts the refusal; a question, a negation, quoted agent text and a notice tag do not. Ready. Landed Nov 5 in batch 10 (59bff081): #1244 scopes a plain Opus ask from the owner's earlier prompts (item 226 b). Open: item 256, whether later prompts may narrow a live grant.
